records.proposedName: The Broken Shell and the Floating Edge
records.summary: Dionasiaʼs surface is a puzzle of dislocated landmasses, shattered crustal plates, and sky-facing chasms. Its geography is not shaped by tectonics or erosion, but by the slow drift of Gravity Wells, the lingering scars of the Great Fracturing, and the upward-pulling void that threatens to reclaim everything. Most of Dionasia's inhabited terrain exists on the underside of cliffs, ridgelines, or mountaintops suspended over vast abyssal skies. Terrain is defined by height, gravitational alignment, proximity to Gravity Wells, and accessibility by skybeast or cable transit.

records.summary: •The Pulse Beneath: A signal—biological or technological—has begun emitting from deep under the Bleeding Pools. Something is waking. •The Spores of Self: A unique fungal species has formed a perfect copy of one party member. It claims to be the real one. •The Root Gate: A massive, overgrown arch covered in stone and flesh occasionally opens to an unknown location. records.summary: “Chaos isnʼt the enemy. Stagnation is.” The Stormlash Veldt isn't about madness or mysticism—itʼs raw, unrefined energy. It rewards speed, ingenuity, and timing. There is a rhythm to survival here—those who fight it are crushed. Those who adapt become charged. Itʼs an ideal zone to test powers gained in earlier zones, to introduce unique weather-linked gear, and to foreshadow upcoming multiversal transitions.

records.proposedName: This Arctic and Taiga Setting in Your Campaign
records.summary: The Arctic Tundra and Taiga environment offers a blend of survival mechanics, exploration, and storytelling. Its extreme weather, limited resources, and isolated nature encourage players to plan ahead, think creatively, and rely on one another. It is an ideal setting for quests focused on endurance, mystery, and discovery. Whether your players are racing against time to escape a blizzard, tracking a mythical beast, or uncovering an ancient civilization beneath the ice, this environment promises excitement and danger. Use shifting weather, resource scarcity, and wildlife encounters to create dynamic challenges that will keep the players engaged and on their toes. This Arctic Tundra and Taiga section equips GMs with everything needed to run an engaging, survival- based adventure in a frozen wilderness. With environmental hazards, ancient mysteries, and encounters with powerful creatures, this setting promises memorable adventures filled with tension, discovery, and danger at every turn.

records.proposedName: This Sandy Desert in Your Campaign
records.summary: The sandy desert environment provides opportunities for survival challenges, moral dilemmas, treasure hunts, and encounters with ancient ruins. The harsh climate forces players to think ahead, conserve resources, and find creative solutions to unexpected problems. This environment is ideal for adventures focused on exploration and endurance, mixing dynamic weather events, environmental hazards, and encounters with strange creatures and factions. The desert can also serve as a narrative bridge between cities or regions, a barrier that must be crossed in order to unlock the next stage of the campaign. Whether the players are hunting a legendary creature, uncovering ancient secrets, or racing against time, the desert offers danger, wonder, and reward at every turn. This Sandy Desert section provides all the tools for GMs and players to create immersive and engaging adventures. With environmental hazards, mirages, ancient ruins, and dangerous creatures, the desert tests both physical endurance and mental resolve—offering unforgettable moments of survival and discovery.

records.summary: •The Arborae did not fight in direct combat but instead used nature as their weapon. •They grew forests back overnight, cutting off goblin supply lines and isolating their forces. •They commanded massive plant creatures, poisoned industrial sites, and altered the land itself to reject goblin structures. •Havalaeaʼs climate turned against the goblins, with monsoons, shifting terrain, and aggressive wildlife acting as additional obstacles. •Arborae warriors, physically connected to the environment, could phase into trees, manipulate roots, and move unseen through their own domain.

records.summary: 1.Camp Layout: •Tents and Shelters: Simple cloth or leather structures provide shelter but are vulnerable to weather and attack. •Fire Pits and Cooking Areas: Centralized for warmth and cooking, these can draw attention or pose a fire hazard if not properly managed. •Supply Wagons: Carry essential goods like food, tools, and medicine, but may be in limited supply and protected by guards. •Livestock Pens: If the camp has animals, they are often kept in makeshift pens, which may attract predators.
